---
title: Client
description: What is SignalGraph's generated client?
---

SignalGraph's CLI generates a client inside the directory specified in the `out` field in `signalgraph.config.ts`.
It exports the client object that the application uses to define the behaviour for each consumer.

An example of the generated client could look like this:
```ts title="Generated client example"
// This file was generated by SignalGraph
// Do not edit this file directly

import * as Runtime from "signalgraph/runtime";
import {
  OrderCreated,
  BillingCompleted,
  Analytics,
  Billing,
  Email
} from "../src/schema/schema.ts";

export type OrdersCreatedPayload = { readonly "orderId": string }

export type BillingCompletedPayload = { readonly "orderId": string }

export type Client =
  Runtime.RuntimeClient &
  {
    ordersCreated: Runtime.RuntimeMessage<OrdersCreatedPayload>;
    billingCompleted: Runtime.RuntimeMessage<BillingCompletedPayload>;
    analytics: Runtime.RuntimeConsumer<OrdersCreatedPayload>;
    billing: Runtime.RuntimeConsumer<OrdersCreatedPayload>;
    email: Runtime.RuntimeConsumer<BillingCompletedPayload>;
  };

const messageGraph = {
  "orders.created": {
    definition: OrderCreated,
    consumers: [Analytics, Billing]
  },
  "billing.completed": {
    definition: BillingCompleted,
    consumers: [Email]
  }
} satisfies Runtime.MessageGraph;

export const Client = Runtime.createClient<Client>(messageGraph);
```

It defines the relations between messages & the consumers that subscribe to it through the message graph which then each adapter uses
to generate their structure. The client also generates specific functions for each message and consumer.

### Handler
For each consumer it generates a handle function with this type signature:
```ts title="Handler type definition"
({ payload, metadata }) => Effect.Effect<void>
```

The payload is the TypeScript type equivalent of the Effect schema that was provided to the consumer's message definition.
The metadata argument contains information about the current message such as message id, correlation id, etc. These shouldn't
be touched unless you know what you are changing!

### Publish
For each message it generates a publish function with this type signature:
```ts title="Publish type definition"
(payload) => Effect.Effect<void>
```

The payload is the TypeScript type equivalent of the Effect schema that was provided to the message definition the publish method lives on.

### Start & Listen

The client also exposes two functions `start` & `listen`. The start function connects to the broker, applies the schema, and creates listeners for each handler.
After that it exits which makes it useful for tests since it does exit early after applying everything.
The listen function on the other hand calls start, and afterwards launches each registered integration as well as suspends the thread.
